judged_text: The helper returns two incompatible shapes — a raw fetch Response in sharing mode versus the provider-specific object (googleauth res, HubspotToken, axios response) otherwise — with an untyped `refreshFunction: () => any` and no defined schema for the sync endpoint's response body. Every integration wired to this helper must guess which shape it will receive; four of the eight call sites in this diff already guess wrong (google, hubspot, zoho-bigin, zohocrm), and each future integration added to the store will repeat the mistake unless the contract is normalized to a parsed token object in both branches.

adjudication.rationale: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns different, incompatible types depending on the branch: in sharing mode it returns a raw `fetch(...)` `Response` (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, lines returning `response` from `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)`), but otherwise it returns whatever the integration-specific `refreshFunction()` returns (gaxios/Google `res`, HubSpot `HubspotToken`, axios response, etc.). Multiple call sites then treat the return value as a provider-shaped object, not a `Response`: e.g. Google uses `const token = res?.data` (`googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`), HubSpot assigns it to `HubspotToken` and reads fields (`hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`), and Zoho Bigin/Zoho CRM read `.data` (`zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts`). If sharing mode is enabled, these will receive a `Response` without `.data`, causing broken refresh behavior. The diff contains no normalization/parsing of the sync endpoint response to match the non-sharing shape.
